note: These changes are authorized only for the unreleased Rust cutover. Any additional divergence is a defect until added here with updated tests and contracts.

entries.oldBehavior: The development database is described by the current EF-generated migration and __EFMigrationsHistory.
entries.newBehavior: Rust v1 starts from one squashed Rust-owned baseline and its own migration history table. EF metadata is not part of the product schema.
entries.reason: Citadel is unreleased and one migration authority is safer than retaining the .NET migration project.
entries.impact: Development and dogfood databases may be reset. A latest-schema converter is optional and is not a release requirement.
entries.proof: Phase 2 clean-install, restart, drift, and baseline tests

entries.oldBehavior: Existing .NET-issued cookies, refresh tokens, setup/OIDC state, and MFA challenges may still be present in development environments.
entries.newBehavior: Rust cutover requires browser reauthentication and does not preserve ephemeral authentication state.
entries.reason: Migrating ephemeral security artifacts increases risk without user value before the first release.
entries.impact: All users sign in again after cutover; durable identities, roles, teams, and access rules remain product behavior.
entries.proof: Phase 3 login, refresh, OIDC, MFA, and authorization matrix tests

entries.oldBehavior: The React client receives SignalR hub messages and group subscriptions.
entries.newBehavior: Rust uses the accepted versioned WebSocket envelope behind the existing frontend realtime adapter.
entries.reason: Rust has no reason to reproduce SignalR framing when subscription, authorization, revision, overflow, and resync semantics can be preserved.
entries.impact: Generated HTTP contracts and frontend resource/query semantics do not change; only the adapter protocol changes at cutover.
entries.proof: Phase 0C protocol tests plus Phase 2-4 frontend reconnect and differential tests

entries.oldBehavior: Handlers are dispatched through Mediator pipelines and persistence is exposed through IUnitOfWork repositories.
entries.newBehavior: Axum routes invoke typed application use cases directly; use cases use explicit SQLx transactions and focused query modules.
entries.reason: Validation, permission, licensing, transaction, and error order are product behavior; framework and locator shapes are not.
entries.impact: No public API or frontend change. Internal extension points based on .NET types are removed.
entries.proof: Phase 2-7 route/use-case authorization and transaction tests

entries.oldBehavior: Current .NET password, token, and encrypted-secret representations are development-era formats.
entries.newBehavior: Rust uses versioned reviewed formats; unreleased environments may re-enter secrets and credentials instead of receiving a general legacy decoder.
entries.reason: A permanent compatibility parser for unreleased crypto formats broadens the attack surface.
entries.impact: The cutover runbook identifies which credentials must be recreated; plaintext is never exported for migration.
entries.proof: Phase 3 crypto vectors, redaction tests, and clean-cutover acceptance

entries.oldBehavior: Core, regular Agent, and Edge Agent are implemented in .NET.
entries.newBehavior: Rust Core continues to interoperate with the active .NET Agents; an Agent rewrite is optional after Core burn-in.
entries.reason: Core-first migration avoids simultaneous control-plane and data-plane replacement.
entries.impact: The shared protobuf sources remain the compatibility boundary. No Agent deployment change is required for the first Rust Core release.
entries.proof: Phase 0B and Phase 4-8 cross-language transport-equivalence tests
